crossRefs.note: “Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!
“My soul is weary of my life. I will give free course to my complaint. I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
Remember my affliction and my misery, the wormwood and the bitterness.
My soul still remembers them, and is bowed down within me.
In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord. My hand was stretched out in the night, and didn’t get tired. My soul…
that he would show you the secrets of wisdom! For true wisdom has two sides. Know therefore that God exacts of you less…

translations.web: “Even today my complaint is rebellious. His hand is heavy in spite of my groaning.
translations.bsb: “Even today my complaint is bitter. His hand is heavy despite my groaning.
translations.kjv: Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning.
translations.asv: Even to-day is my complaint rebellious: My stroke is heavier than my groaning.
